title: WebWork Integration Monitoring
description: Availability, traffic, latency, rate limiting, errors and jobs for the WebWork integration. Metrics come from backend/utils/webworkMetrics.js and logs from backend/utils/webworkLogger.js in the performance-tracker repo.

panels.title: Integration status
panels.description: Reflects the last call each process actually made. It does not decay with silence: no traffic holds the last known state instead of reporting an outage. Empty until the first call after a restart.

panels.title: Since last success
panels.description: Age of the most recent successful call across processes.

panels.title: Success rate
panels.description: Share of calls answered with 2xx or 3xx over the selected range.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: or vector(0) so a clean period renders 0 rather than "No data", which would be indistinguishable from a broken scrape.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(webwork_errors_total{job=~"$job", endpoint=~"$endpoint", method=~"$method"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(webwork_requests_total{job=~"$job", endpoint=~"$endpoint", method=~"$method"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Requests / min
panels.description: WebWork's documented ceiling is 60/min per workspace.

panels.title: HTTP 429 (range)
panels.description: Rate-limited responses over the selected range.

panels.title: In flight
panels.description: Calls started and not yet settled. With no timeout in the client, a number that stays high is the signature of hung requests.

panels.title: Consecutive failures
panels.description: Failed calls since the last success, worst process. Rises the moment WebWork starts refusing and drops to zero on the first success — the fastest signal that the integration is in trouble.

panels.title: Consecutive successes
panels.description: Successful calls since the last failure, weakest process. Useful to confirm a recovery actually held rather than flapping.

panels.title: Job: time since last success
panels.description: The reconcile job runs nightly at 03:00 UTC, so anything past ~24h means a run was missed or failed.

panels.title: Job runs by status
panels.description: Terminal status of each execution.

panels.title: Requests over time
panels.description: Total call rate after the dashboard filters.

panels.title: Most called endpoints
panels.description: Call count per normalized endpoint over the selected range.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (endpoint) (increase(webwork_requests_total{job=~"$job", endpoint=~"$endpoint", method=~"$method", status=~"$status"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Requests by status code
panels.description: status="none" means the call never got a response — a timeout or a socket failure.

panels.title: Call volume by hour of day
panels.description: Hourly totals across the selected range. The reconcile job at 03:00 UTC and the morning provisioning rush should stand out as bands.

panels.title: Latency percentiles
panels.description: The mean is included because a percentile alone hides a bimodal distribution.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, endpoint) (rate(webwork_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", endpoint=~"$endpoint", method=~"$method"}[$__range]))))

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: Concurrency against WebWork. Sustained growth with no matching request rate means calls are hanging.

panels.title: Time spent awaiting WebWork
panels.description: Cumulative wait divided by wall clock. A value above 1 means calls overlap; it is effectively the average number of calls in flight.

panels.title: HTTP 429 over time
panels.description: When these appear tells you which job or rush hit the ceiling.

panels.title: Endpoints hit hardest by rate limiting
Retry-After advertised by WebWork
panels.description: Only populated when WebWork sends the header. Nothing consumes it yet — the client has no backoff — so this is the budget a future retry would have to respect.

panels.title: Attempts per operation
panels.description: Attempts an operation actually made. Above 1 means pagination, not a retry loop: the client has no retry. A caller retrying shows up here too.

panels.title: Rate limit events
panels.description: pino lines where rate_limited is true, carrying the endpoint, the Retry-After value and the correlation id.

panels.title: Errors over time
panels.description: http_4xx / http_5xx / rate_limited / timeout / connection / unexpected.

panels.title: Transport failures
panels.description: Failures with no HTTP response. The client sets no timeout, so a "timeout" here is undici's own default rather than a deadline we chose.

panels.title: WebWork logs
panels.description: module is a field inside the pino JSON, not a Loki stream label — the labels are job, stream, host and filename — so it has to be matched after | json, never as {module="webwork"}, which silently returns nothing. Drop the outcome filter to see successes too.

panels.title: Currently running
panels.description: The cron is overlap-guarded, so anything above 1 means two processes are running it at once — expected with multiple instances, worth checking otherwise.

panels.title: WebWork calls per job execution
panels.description: How much WebWork traffic one reconcile run generates — the number to watch against the 60/min ceiling.

panels.title: Job logs
panels.description: Start, completion and failure lines for the reconcile job, with duration, record counts and the JobExecution id.
